title: KMS Alerting Review & Tuning (Draft) — latency/error spikes, breaker state, and paging policy
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-21 (AG)

Owner: Allison Grant (Observability)
Reviewers: Sean Gallagher (SRE), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Emily Zhao (data-plane), Vikram Singh (data-plane), Marcus Lin (Security)

Purpose
This doc proposes a tuned, low-noise alerting policy for KMS dependency health across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The intent is to detect KMS brownouts early (timeouts/throttling/AccessDenied/disabled keys/region endpoint issues) while avoiding alert fatigue from transient provider hiccups and from expected rotation behavior (dual-read windows).

Non-goals
- This is not a full runbook. See: KMS dependency degradation runbook (Confluence).
- This is not a replacement for audit logging requirements; this doc focuses on operational alerts/metrics.

Background / what changed recently
- Data plane now has standardized retry/backoff + circuit breaker for KMS calls (PR 28741).
- Rotation adds bounded dual-read (try new key, then old) window (PR 28822), which can temporarily increase KMS traffic and change error distributions.
- We are adding per-tenant KMS health summary endpoint for ops/debug (PR 28910) which should reduce time-to-triage.
- Failure-mode harness/game day (ENG-4234 / ENG-4258) will validate these signals.

Alerting principles (agreed direction)
1) Page only on customer-impacting symptoms OR a high-confidence precursor that historically leads to impact.
2) Prefer multi-signal pages (e.g., KMS timeout + breaker open + decrypt failure) vs single noisy indicators.
3) Separate “provider degraded” from “our configuration/permissions broken” (AccessDenied / NotFound / disabled key).
4) Include tenant segmentation where possible (top impacted tenants + deployment mode) and avoid leaking sensitive identifiers in broad channels.
5) Every page must include: which provider/region, which operation (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey), breaker state, retry saturation, cache hit rate, and suggested immediate mitigation toggles.

Canonical metrics (naming suggestions)
NOTE: names below reflect what we should standardize in dashboards; implementation may differ by service. The important part is consistent labels.

KMS client metrics (data plane)
- kms_request_total{provider,operation,region,service,tenant_tier,deploy_mode}
- kms_request_latency_ms_bucket{provider,operation,region,service}
  - Primary views: p50/p95/p99
- kms_request_errors_total{provider,operation,region,service,error_code}
  - error_code normalized across SDKs where possible:
    - Timeout / DeadlineExceeded
    - Throttling / TooManyRequests
    - AccessDenied / PermissionDenied
    - NotFound (key/alias)
    - DisabledKey / InvalidState
    - Internal / ServiceUnavailable
    - Unknown
- kms_retries_total{provider,operation,region,service}
- kms_retry_exhausted_total{provider,operation,region,service}
- kms_circuit_breaker_state{provider,region,service} (0=closed, 1=half_open, 2=open)
- kms_circuit_breaker_open_total{provider,region,service}
- kms_circuit_breaker_open_duration_ms{provider,region,service}
- kms_cache_hit_total{cache_type=dek|kek_metadata,service}
- kms_cache_miss_total{cache_type=dek|kek_metadata,service}
- kms_cache_stale_served_total{cache_type,service} (if supported in degradation mode)

Service-level impact metrics
- encrypt_failure_rate = encrypt_failures / encrypt_attempts (per service)
- decrypt_failure_rate = decrypt_failures / decrypt_attempts (per service)
- token_request_error_rate (to correlate customer symptom spikes)
- p95 request latency at API boundary for endpoints that depend on KMS at request time (should be rare; ideally only on cache miss)

Audit/event stream (for correlation, not paging)
- KMSDecryptFailed audit events volume by error_code (from audit pipeline)
- KMSKeyPolicyDenied events volume

Recommended dashboards (examples)
Dashboard A: “KMS Dependency Overview (Global)”
- Row 1: KMS latency p95/p99 by provider+region (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey tabs)
- Row 2: Error rate by error_code stacked area (normalized)
- Row 3: Circuit breaker state over time (open/half-open), plus open count
- Row 4: Retry metrics (retries/request, retry_exhausted)
- Row 5: Cache hit rate (DEK cache + KEK metadata cache), and estimated KMS QPS avoided
- Row 6: Top impacted services/tenants (sanitized) by decrypt failures and by breaker-open time

Dashboard B: “KMS Customer Impact (Hosted/Dedicated)”
- Decrypt failures and downstream request failure correlations
- By tenant_tier (enterprise vs self-serve) and by region
- “Is this an internal regression?” panel: deploy version overlay + feature flag state overlay

Dashboard C: “Private Deployments — KMS Health (Per Cluster)” (restricted)
- Same as A but per-cluster, with additional panels:
  - IAM/permission failures (AccessDenied) rate
  - Key state failures (DisabledKey/InvalidState)
  - Region endpoint mismatch suspects (high NotFound/InvalidState during install/upgrade)
- Linkout: per-tenant/cluster KMS health summary endpoint (admin gated)

Dashboard D: “Rotation Window Monitoring”
- Dual-read attempts rate
- New-key decrypt success vs old-key fallback rate
- Bounded fallback limit reached count
- KMS QPS delta during rotation
- AccessDenied spikes on new key (misconfigured key policy)

Paging policy (proposed)
Severity definitions
- SEV2 page: High likelihood of customer impact within minutes OR active customer impact affecting multiple tenants/regions.
- SEV3 page: Limited customer impact (single region or small segment) OR precursor with strong confidence.
- Ticket only: Degraded signals without impact, slow-burning trends, or configuration issues confined to a single tenant (unless enterprise / SLA).

Proposed alerts (initial thresholds; tune after game day + 1–2 weeks of real traffic)
All alerts should include labels: provider, region, operation, deploy_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), service.

1) KMS Decrypt Customer Impact (page, SEV2)
Condition (any deploy_mode):
- decrypt_failure_rate > 0.10% for 5 minutes AND decrypt_attempts >= 5k in that window
AND (one of):
- kms_circuit_breaker_state == open for >= 2 minutes
- kms_request_latency_p99 > 1500ms for 5 minutes
- kms_retry_exhausted_total increasing sharply (>= 50/min)
Notes:
- 0.10% is intentionally low for decrypt; decrypt failures tend to be directly customer-visible and should be near-zero. We can raise to 0.25% if noisy during known rotations.

2) KMS Timeout/Throttling Brownout (page, SEV3)
Condition:
- kms_request_errors_total{error_code=Timeout|Throttling} / kms_request_total > 2% for 10 minutes
AND kms_request_total >= 10k in that window
AND (breaker opens >= 1 OR p99 latency > 2000ms)
Notes:
- This is the “provider brownout” detector. We page SEV3 because some brownouts self-resolve; runbook includes cache TTL and breaker tuning toggles.

3) Circuit Breaker Sustained Open (page, SEV3; upgrade to SEV2 if coupled with decrypt failures)
Condition:
- kms_circuit_breaker_state == open for >= 10 minutes in any region
AND kms_request_total >= 1k/10m
Rationale:
- Sustained open likely indicates a real provider outage or a code/config regression. The breaker is expected to flap briefly; we’re targeting sustained open.

4) AccessDenied / PermissionDenied Spike (ticket; page for enterprise/private install)
Default (ticket):
- kms_request_errors_total{error_code=AccessDenied} / kms_request_total > 0.5% for 10 minutes
- Include top impacted tenant(s) via health summary endpoint (restricted) and recent config changes.
Escalation to page (SEV3) when:
- deploy_mode=private AND affects >= 3 clusters OR appears after a release/upgrade
- OR tenant_tier=enterprise AND decrypt failures > 0.05% for 5 minutes
Rationale:
- AccessDenied is often a customer/IAM config issue in Private; should not page global on-call unless it’s systemic.

5) DisabledKey / InvalidState / NotFound (ticket; page if widespread)
Ticket:
- error_code in (DisabledKey, InvalidState, NotFound) > 10/min for 15 minutes (per provider/region)
Page (SEV3) if:
- >= 5 tenants affected (hosted/dedicated) OR >= 3 private clusters OR coincident with rotation window start
Rationale:
- These are typically misconfiguration or an automation bug, and they’re actionable but not always urgent unless widespread.

6) Cache Hit Rate Regression (ticket)
Condition:
- DEK cache hit rate drops by > 20% absolute compared to 7-day baseline for 30 minutes
AND KMS QPS increases > 30% compared to baseline
Notes:
- This is a precursor alert; it catches “we accidentally disabled caching / reduced TTL too far / cache stampede” before it becomes latency/errors.

7) KMS Health Summary Endpoint Disagreement (ticket)
Condition:
- health summary indicates degraded for >= 30 minutes but global KMS metrics show normal OR vice versa
Rationale:
- Catches instrumentation gaps/labeling errors and ensures the on-call debug endpoint stays reliable.

Routing: who gets paged
- Primary: SRE on-call (global)
- Secondary (auto add to incident channel when page fires): Security on-call (Marcus Lin rotation) for AccessDenied/rotation-related pages; Data-plane engineer on-call for latency/breaker pages (Emily Zhao / Vikram Singh rotation)
- For Private-only issues: Private deployments on-call rotation (via #eng-private-oncall) + Solutions Eng if customer escalation is required

Notification content (must-have fields)
Every KMS page should render:
- Provider + region + operation(s)
- Error code distribution (top 3)
- p95/p99 latency
- Breaker state + open duration
- Retry exhausted rate
- Cache hit rate
- Top impacted tenants/services (sanitized; link to restricted view)
- Links: Dashboard A + relevant runbook section + incident-bot KMS snippet

Tuning notes / expected noise sources
- Rotation dual-read windows increase decrypt attempts and may temporarily increase KMS traffic; alerts must include “rotation flag enabled?” indicator.
- IAM propagation delays (Private install/upgrade) can cause short-lived AccessDenied. Ticket thresholds should be forgiving; page only when systemic or enterprise impact.
- Provider throttling can be bursty; we should prefer 10-minute windows for brownout pages to avoid paging on brief spikes.

Open questions
1) What is the maximum acceptable p99 latency for KMS calls before we consider it a user-impact precursor? (Proposed: 1.5s; validate in game day)
2) Should we add an explicit “KMS spend/QPS anomaly” alert to catch runaway loops? (Maybe: KMS QPS > 2x baseline for 15m)
3) Tenant segmentation: do we need “enterprise-only” alert views by default, or only in restricted dashboards?

Action items (next steps)
- [AG] Align metric names/labels with data-plane team (ENG-4239) so dashboards/alerts are consistent across services.
- [SG/RM] Dry-run these thresholds during failure-mode harness (ENG-4234) and game day (ENG-4258); record false positives/negatives.
- [EZ/VS] Confirm circuit breaker open/half-open telemetry is reliable and exported per region/provider.
- [CO] Ensure incident-bot template includes the must-have fields and links (PR 221).
- [ML/KO] Sanity check that alert payloads don’t include sensitive identifiers in non-restricted channels (Private clusters/tenants).

Appendix: initial threshold rationale (quick)
- Decrypt failures: extremely sensitive; small rates can be widespread impact when decrypt sits on hot path for certain artifacts.
- Timeout/throttling: common provider symptom; page only when sustained and correlated with breaker/latency.
- AccessDenied/DisabledKey: usually configuration, but becomes urgent if it’s a rollout regression or it blocks rotation.

Appendix: example incident timeline mapping
- Provider brownout: throttling spikes → retries rise → breaker flaps → p99 climbs → decrypt failures increase. We want to page at “breaker sustained open” + “timeout/throttle sustained” before decrypt failures exceed 0.10%.
- Customer misconfig in Private: AccessDenied only in one cluster; health summary flags single cluster; ticket to Private on-call + customer instructions; do not page global.
